name: Edit-survival rate
definition: Share of engine-drafted text that survives, unchanged in substance, from the first drafted revision to the submitted document.
formula: surviving_drafted_chars / total_drafted_chars, computed per section then weighted by section length; substance-preserving whitespace and formatting edits excluded.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Rises when reviewers disengage as easily as when quality improves. Read next to review_rounds_to_accept and reviewer_hours_per_proposal — survival up with hours flat is disengagement, not improvement.

name: Edit reason mix
definition: Distribution of reviewer edits across reason codes: factual, tone, length, structure, strategy, compliance, other.
formula: count(edits by reason) / count(all edits), per period.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Diagnostic, not evaluative — a shift toward 'tone' is a voice-spec problem and a shift toward 'factual' is a KB problem. They need opposite fixes, so the mix matters more than the total.

name: Review rounds to acceptance
definition: Number of full review passes a section goes through before a reviewer accepts it.
formula: max(revision) at accept event, per section; reported as median and 90th percentile.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Compare against the WP-Zero baseline round count; without it the number has no scale.

name: Tier-1 block rate
definition: Share of drafted sections containing at least one Tier-1 bindable claim that the Claim Auditor blocked pending verification.
formula: sections_with_tier1_block / sections_drafted.

reliability.known_failure_mode: A falling block rate is equally consistent with a better Fact Sheet and with an auditor that stopped catching things. Only interpretable beside poison-set recall from the eval suite (E2).

name: Tier-1 waiver rate
definition: Share of Tier-1 blocks released by human waiver rather than by verification.
formula: blocks_waived / blocks_raised.

reliability.known_failure_mode: A high waiver rate means the blocking control has become a click-through. A waiver with an empty reason string is an alert, not a data point.

alerting.condition: waiver recorded with empty or boilerplate waiver_reason

name: False-gap rate
definition: Share of gaps raised to a human where the answer was in fact retrievable from the KB at the time of the run.
formula: gaps_resolved_from_existing_kb / gaps_raised.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Over-flagging trains reviewers to click past gap pings, silently disabling the invention guard (decision E3).

name: Gap resolution time
definition: Elapsed hours from a gap ping being sent to a human answer being recorded.
formula: gap.answered_at - gap.pinged_at, reported as median and share unanswered past the escalation threshold.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Median hides the tail; the unanswered-past-escalation share is the number that predicts a stalled pursuit.

alerting.condition: gap unanswered past escalation threshold (decision N4)

name: Red-team score
definition: Adversarial reviewer-agent score on the annotated draft, on the calibrated rubric.
formula: Mean rubric score across scored sections; judge model and rubric_id recorded with every value.

reliability.known_failure_mode: An uncalibrated judge is a random number generator with a confident tone (E5). The series breaks at any judge-model change — segment, never splice.

name: Engine cost per pursuit
definition: Direct model API spend for all runs belonging to a pursuit.
formula: sum(agent_call.cost_usd) over the pursuit's live runs; equals sum of run.totals.cost_usd.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Never a headline. Reported alone it makes the engine look cheap while reviewer hours — orders of magnitude larger — go unmeasured. Always a component of blended_cost_per_proposal.

alerting.condition: exceeds soft per-pursuit budget by 50%, or circuit breaker trips (N6)

name: Engine cost per section
definition: Direct model spend attributable to drafting and validating one section.
formula: sum(agent_call.cost_usd) grouped by target.section_id.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Useful mainly as an outlier detector — the section type costing many times the median is usually a retry loop or a runaway retrieval, not expensive content.

name: Reviewer hours per proposal
definition: Total human time on task across all reviewers for one pursuit, from first gate to submission.
formula: sum(review_session.active_ms) / 3.6e6, plus gate-close confirmed adjustments; grouped by actor_role.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Passive timing undercounts offline review and overcounts an idle open tab; the 90-second idle timeout and the gate-close confirmation are the corrections. Aggregate by role only — never by named person outside the reviewer's own view.

name: Human cost per proposal
definition: Reviewer hours by role priced at the loaded rate card.
formula: sum over roles of (reviewer_hours[role] * loaded_rate[role]); rate_card_version recorded with every value.

reliability.known_failure_mode: A rate-card revision reads as a productivity change unless the version is pinned and annotated on the trend.

name: Blended cost per submitted proposal
definition: Engine spend plus priced reviewer time, per proposal actually submitted. The decision-grade cost figure.
formula: (engine_cost + human_cost) / submissions in period; abandoned pursuits reported as a separate line, not folded in silently.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Meaningless without the WP-Zero baseline to compare against — that is what makes baseline capture the one unrecoverable item (N1).

name: Cost delta vs. human baseline
definition: Blended cost per proposal as a ratio of the pre-pilot human baseline cost per proposal.
formula: blended_cost_per_proposal / baseline_cost_per_proposal, matched on comparable pursuit type and size.

reliability.confidence_caveat: Baseline is drawn from 3–5 past pursuits and carries its own variance; treat differences under ~20% as indistinguishable.
reliability.known_failure_mode: Pursuit-to-pursuit variance in size and complexity swamps small deltas — match on comparable pursuits or say so.

name: Response cost as basis points of pursued value
definition: Blended response cost expressed against the estimated contract value of the pursuit.
formula: (blended_cost / estimated_contract_value) * 10000.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Depends on a CRM estimate that is itself a guess early in a pursuit; useful for proportionality, not for precision.

name: Blended cost per win
definition: Total blended response cost across all pursuits in a period divided by wins recorded in that period.
formula: sum(blended_cost over pursuits in period) / count(wins in period).

reliability.confidence_caveat: Lagging by the full sales cycle and dominated by win-rate noise at pilot volume. A curiosity for the first two years, not a KPI.
reliability.known_failure_mode: Reads as a productivity metric when it is mostly a measure of which deals happened to close.

name: Cycle time, receipt to submission
definition: Calendar days from RFP receipt to submission.
formula: submission_date - receipt_date, per pursuit.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Bounded below by the buyer's deadline, not by the engine — a team that finishes early still submits on the due date, so improvement shows up as slack, not as a shorter cycle.

name: Compute time vs. human wait
definition: Split of elapsed run time into engine compute and time waiting on a human (gates and gap answers).
formula: run.totals.compute_ms and run.totals.human_wait_ms; wall_ms = compute_ms + human_wait_ms.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Reported as a single elapsed number it measures reviewers' calendars and calls it engine latency (decision O6).

name: Prompt cache hit ratio
definition: Share of input tokens served from prompt cache.
formula: sum(tokens.cache_read) / sum(tokens.input + tokens.cache_read).

reliability.known_failure_mode: The cheapest real lever on engine cost and usually worth more than a model downgrade — but a high ratio on a low-volume day means nothing.

name: Agent retry rate
definition: Share of agent calls that required at least one retry.
formula: count(agent_call where retries > 0) / count(agent_call).

reliability.known_failure_mode: Retries are where silent cost lives; a retry storm shows up in spend long before it shows up in quality.

name: Flywheel yield
definition: Proposals the flywheel generated from reviewer feedback, and how many a steward accepted.
formula: counts of flywheel_routing.action_taken by outcome (proposed / accepted / rejected), per period.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Volume of proposals is a vanity counter on its own; acceptance rate and the lesson-to-draft lag are the signal.

name: Lesson-to-draft lag
definition: Days from a reviewer edit being recorded to the corresponding lesson appearing in a subsequent draft.
formula: median(first_subsequent_citation_date - feedback_event.at) for accepted flywheel writes.

reliability.known_failure_mode: The actual measure of whether the flywheel turns. A healthy proposal count with an unbounded lag means the flywheel is a suggestion box.

name: KB citation coverage
definition: Share of KB cards cited in at least one draft over the trailing twelve months.
formula: distinct(kb.cards_cited over 12 months) / count(active cards).

reliability.known_failure_mode: Low coverage can mean dead weight in the corpus or a retrieval problem; check against mapper recall before pruning anything.

name: Fact Sheet staleness
definition: Count and share of governed Tier-1 facts past their review date.
formula: count(facts where review_due < today) / count(active facts).

reliability.known_failure_mode: Stale governed facts are worse than missing ones — the auditor verifies against them and passes a claim that is no longer true.

alerting.condition: any certification or insurance fact past review date

name: Win rate
definition: Share of submitted proposals that resulted in a win.
formula: wins / submissions, per period.

reliability.confidence_caveat: At 10–20 pursuits a year a win-rate change will never reach statistical significance. 30% to 40% on eighteen pursuits is two extra wins and well inside noise. Displayed with n and this caveat, always.
reliability.known_failure_mode: Staking the business case on demonstrated win-rate lift guarantees the case fails — not because the engine does not work, but because the sample cannot speak.

name: Submission volume and no-bid mix
definition: Proposals submitted, pursuits abandoned, and opportunities no-bid in a period.
formula: counts by disposition.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Capacity gains show up here before they show up anywhere else — and so does the failure mode where cheap responses drive up bids that should have been no-bids.

name: Run success rate
definition: Share of live runs that complete without an unrecovered failure.
formula: runs with run.status == 'completed' / live runs started; resume events counted separately.

reliability.known_failure_mode: A high success rate with frequent resumes is a reliability problem wearing a clean shirt — report resume count beside it (N2).

name: Anonymization & leakage scan result
definition: Pass/fail of ingestion-time anonymization and the pre-export leakage scan against the restricted provenance index.
formula: Boolean per scan. Any failure is an incident, not a trend point.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Averaging this into a percentage is itself the mistake — the required recall is 1.00 with no waiver (E4), so the only meaningful values are 'clean' and 'incident'.

alerting.route_to: named human owner — incident path, not a digest

name: Eval suite pass state
definition: Pass/fail state of every blocking eval bar at the currently deployed release.
formula: Per-bar result from the last full suite run attached to the release record (E7).

reliability.known_failure_mode: A green board against an uncalibrated judge is decoration; calibration date is displayed with the board.

name: Injection screen flags
definition: Injection-screen flags raised on intake documents (S2/T1). Any flag is reviewed at Gate 1; the count is context, not a target.
formula: count(validation records where check == 'injection_screen' and result == 'flag'), per run.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Zero forever means the screen is dead, not that buyers are polite — the planted-string regression test is the liveness check.

name: Card-catalog scan share of run cost
definition: Share of a run's token cost consumed by the first step of card-catalog retrieval — scanning the catalog — rather than by opening and using the documents it selects. The trigger metric for the retrieval ceiling.
formula: catalog_scan_tokens_cost / run.totals.cost_usd, per run; catalog scan identified by the retrieval step marker on agent_call records.

reliability.known_failure_mode: A share, so it falls when anything else gets more expensive. A retry storm makes retrieval look efficient. Read beside catalog_size in absolute terms — the ceiling is driven by corpus growth, not by the ratio.

alerting.condition: sustained above 0.20 over a reporting period

name: Extraction fabrication count
definition: Count of table cells present in one extraction path and absent or differing in the other, when the same document is extracted both deterministically and by the vision-language path. A non-zero count in the production path means the extractor invented content.
formula: count of cell-level diffs between deterministic and VLM extraction of the same table; reported as a raw count, never as a rate.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Detects disagreement, not truth: if both paths fabricate the same cell, the count is zero. It is a tripwire, not a proof of correctness, and it only fires where a labeled or paired comparison exists.

alerting.condition: any non-zero count in the production extraction path

name: Extraction seconds per page
definition: Wall-clock extraction time per page of source document, on production hardware. The throughput watch on the extraction layer, which is a cost accepted for quality rather than a gain.
formula: extraction_wall_ms / page_count, per document; report p50 and p95, never the mean.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Improves dramatically and misleadingly once the content-digest cache warms. Cache hits are filtered out of this metric for that reason; watch cache_hit_ratio separately.

alerting.condition: p95 > 5000ms per page on target hardware

name: Extraction table fidelity
definition: Cell-level agreement between extracted tables and hand-labeled ground truth on the extraction bench. The standing quality signal for the document extraction layer.
formula: matching_cells / total_labeled_cells, reported separately for simple and complex (merged/nested-header/multi-page) tables; never averaged across the two.

reliability.known_failure_mode: Measured only against the labeled bench, which is small and hand-built. A high score means the extractor handles the documents someone thought to label — not the next scanned solicitation. Refresh the bench whenever a production document defeats it.

name: Manual document-prep hours per pursuit
definition: Human time spent preparing buyer documents for the engine — transcribing requirement or compliance matrices, retyping tables, cleaning scans, restructuring forms. Layer 2 of the cost model, and the business claim the extraction layer is meant to satisfy.
formula: sum of feedback_event.effort.active_ms where effort.scope == 'document_prep', converted to hours, per pursuit; reviewer-confirmed figures preferred over passive where both exist.

reliability.confidence_caveat: Passively measured and labeled as estimated. Requires the document_prep effort scope to be live before the pilot — this work disappears once extraction improves, and cannot be reconstructed after the fact.
reliability.known_failure_mode: Goes to zero for the honest reason (nobody transcribes any more) and the dishonest one (people stopped logging it, or moved the work outside the tool). Read next to reviewer_hours_per_proposal: prep falling while total hours hold flat means the work moved, not vanished.
